Operator

Good morning, and welcome to the Kestrel Analytics second quarter 2026 earnings call. I will now turn the call over to Sofia Marquez, Head of Investor Relations.

Sofia Marquez

Thank you, and good morning. With me today are Daniel Okafor, our Chief Executive Officer, and Helen Ortiz, our Chief Financial Officer.

Today's remarks include forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties, and actual results could differ materially from those we describe. Please see our filings with the SEC for more information.

I will now hand the call to Daniel.

Daniel Okafor

Thanks, Sofia. Revenue for the quarter was $120.4 million, up 9% from a year ago. Subscription revenue grew 14% and now makes up 71% of total revenue.

Our finance team did excellent work this quarter.
Helen Ortiz and her team closed the books two days earlier than last year.

Helen Ortiz, our Chief Financial Officer, will now walk through the numbers in more detail.

Helen Ortiz - Chief Financial Officer

Thank you, Daniel. Gross margin was 63.5%, up 80 basis points. Operating income was $18.2 million. For the full year, we now expect revenue of $480 million to $490 million.

We remain cautious about enterprise budgets in the second half.

Operator

Thank you. We will now open the line for questions. Our first question comes from Ravi Menon with Bank of Examples.

Ravi Menon

Thanks. How much of the subscription growth came from new customers versus expansion?

Daniel Okafor

About 60% came from expansion within existing customers.

Operator

Our next question comes from Claire Dubois with Fictional Securities.

Claire Dubois

Can you say more about what drives the caution on enterprise budgets?

Helen Ortiz

Some large customers are taking longer to approve renewals. We have not seen cancellations.

Operator

That concludes our question-and-answer session. I will turn the call back to Daniel Okafor for closing remarks.

Daniel Okafor

Thank you all for joining. We look forward to speaking with you next quarter.
